title: Sending Reputation: What Changes When You Control the Infrastructure
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: Gmail monitors domain and IP reputation. Google states that other senders' activity on a shared IP can affect everyone using it. That is a reason to understand your sending path, not proof that every shared service performs badly.
content:
Domain and IP reputation are different

Gmail monitors domain and IP reputation. Google states that other senders' activity on a shared IP can affect everyone using it. That is a reason to understand your sending path, not proof that every shared service performs badly.

Self-hosting the app does not choose the relay

Your campaign database can run on your server while outgoing mail uses a shared provider. Trace the actual sending service before claiming a dedicated reputation. Moving the app does not automatically move an IP or export a provider's internal reputation data.

Control brings work

Authentication, recipient consent, unsubscribes, bounce handling and stable sending volume still matter. A dedicated IP does not make unwanted mail wanted. Google recommends monitoring Postmaster Tools and reducing volume when delivery problems appear.

Measure instead of assuming

Keep a record of the sending domain, relay, authentication results and relevant delivery signals for each campaign. Compare your own traffic over time rather than promising that owning a server guarantees inbox placement.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
